caption: Conceptual drift-to-search overview. Current forecasting and spatial regression of currents and density support a three-dimensional passive-motion prediction constrained above the seabed. Its horizontal location centers an assumed Manhattan-distance Poisson-shell search field. Two maps preserve the same coordinates: an unsuccessful parallel sweep adds D4 to the excluded set, while a later predicted position supplies the adjacent center and the next search assignment. Permanent exclusion depends on the paper's perfect-detection and no-reentry approximations; assignments change only between intervals and inter-cell transit is neglected. Cells and shading illustrate the mechanism rather than computed probabilities; the approximately 300 m cell and 30 min interval are the paper's example assumptions.
placement: End of Introduction, before model definitions; focused overview of the drift-to-search mechanism rather than an inventory of all three paper models.

source_notes.locator: PDF p11, Equation 18; original page visually inspected
source_notes.issue: x and y acceleration equations both contain -F_R cos(phi) cos(theta), although the text introduces the azimuth angle for horizontal decomposition.
source_notes.handling: Record as source inconsistency. Print neither copied nor silently repaired component equations; use qualitative hull forces and a conceptual trajectory.

source_notes.locator: PDF p17, Equation 26; original page visually inspected
source_notes.issue: y_G is printed as INT(N/M) + G_s/2, without the grid-size multiplier present in the x-center expression.
source_notes.handling: Do not reproduce or certify the formula. Use explicit editorial cell identities A-G and 1-7 in matched conceptual grids.

source_notes.locator: PDF p18 Equation 30 versus PDF p19 Equations 34-35; both original pages visually inspected
source_notes.issue: Equation 30 divides Poisson shell mass by N_4 for an individual cell; Equations 34-35 subsequently use a shell Poisson mass for a cell without that factor.
source_notes.handling: State assumed shell organization and per-shell sharing qualitatively. No numerical probability array, per-cell formula, or calculated posterior is produced.

source_notes.locator: PDF p19, Section 7.3 and Equation 35; original page visually inspected
source_notes.issue: Event B is described as the target outside searched regions; the final denominator prose calls p(B) the total prior probability of all searched grids and says it decreases as search expands.
source_notes.handling: Show intended no-detection elimination and qualitative weight update only. Explicitly avoid silently normalizing/correcting the source or claiming implementation validation.

source_notes.issue: Small movement relative to cell width is used to justify permanent zero probability after search; it does not logically preclude boundary crossing or later re-entry.
source_notes.handling: Visible no-re-entry assumption. Forecast dots straddle one common cell boundary by a small distance; excluded cells remain fixed. No claim that no-reentry follows as a physical theorem.

source_notes.issue: The prose asserts the center is most probable and probability decreases with distance, while a Poisson law with changing intensity does not by itself ensure universal shell-mass monotonicity.
source_notes.handling: Schematic early ordering and qualitative tones only. No universal monotonicity claim, numeric legend, or computed distribution.

source_notes.locator: PDF p9, Equation 12 and adjacent prose; text read
source_notes.issue: The displayed ridge objective omits a regularization coefficient, while the prose introduces alpha and the software discussion uses lambda.
source_notes.handling: Method name only; no objective formula in the figure.

source_notes.locator: PDF p1 summary versus PDF pp15-16 Section 6.4/Table 8; text read

source_notes.locator: PDF p16 equipment schemes versus PDF p18 Equation 31 prose; text read
